usageNotes: Retrieves the current time from inside a running VM via the QEMU Guest Agent. The VM must be running and have the guest agent installed and active; the call will fail if the agent is not responding. Useful for detecting time drift between the VM and the host without logging into the guest.

examples.summary: Get the current guest time from VM 101 on node pve1

tips: The returned `result` object typically contains `localtime`, `timezone`, and `utctime` fields from the guest OS.
If the guest agent is not running, Proxmox returns a 500 error — check agent status with get_nodes_node_qemu_vmid_agent_info first.
Time drift between guest and host is common on VMs that were suspended or migrated; compare utctime against host time to detect skew.
Requires VM.GuestAgent.Audit or VM.GuestAgent.Unrestricted on /vms/{vmid} — either privilege satisfies the check.
